definition: Self-play is a technique for improving the performance of reinforcement learning agents.
details: Intuitively, agents learn to improve their performance by playing "against themselves".

explainer.lead: Self-play is a reinforcement learning technique in which agents improve their performance by playing against themselves. It matters because it generates a training opponent without external data.

tiers.eli5: Two players who are both you: every match makes both of you a little better.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to let reinforcement learning agents improve by competing against themselves. A pitfall is that an agent only learns to beat the opponent it faces, so the self-generated challenge shapes what it learns.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it is a technique for improving reinforcement learning agents in which agents learn by playing against themselves. Its scope is limited to settings where self-competition provides a meaningful training signal.

explainer.example: A game-playing agent repeatedly plays matches against a copy of itself, and its performance improves through those matches.
